conclusion: The constant-x=-27.25 R523/R152 seam is artificial, but there IS a real diagonal northern retaining/bank edge. Lower floor is continuous across x=-27.25 south of y~0.1; near y~0.2..0.5 it meets a steep edge and upper sloped ground. Extending the lower R523 plane north to y1.175 would erase this real edge. Stable-control absence northward was caused by the <18cm cell-range filter, not missing raw class2 data.

recommendedDomain.westwardSupport: up to5.75m west of seam inside the hull; northward hull tapers to x~-29.4 at y~-1.6, so do not treat as rectangular support.
recommendedDomain.construction: Independently model lower grade, upper grade and a closed steep retaining/bank connector along the measured diagonal edge; join existing authored terrain across the lower-floor seam southward. Preserve the diagonal height break, not the old rectangular seam.

limits: Class2 is a ground classification, not a survey-guaranteed facade or retaining-wall classification. Near-edge points provide level brackets; steep connector material/type should follow visible source.

ACT corroborates a near-vertical break at x=-28..-27; its absolute floor is 0.2–0.5m above class2 locally, and western x=-30/-31 scan is smeared into a ramp. Use class2 for elevation and ACT only for edge topology.

Upper slope plane controls lie y1.2..3.8; extending to a diagonal edge south of y1.2 is not independently validated by the quoted heldout test. Raw near-edge upper points support the existence and levels, with local curvature.
Do not use all northern mixed-height points in a single smooth fit.
